questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following organelles is bounded by a double membrane and contains its own circular DNA?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have an inner and outer membrane and possess their own circular DNA, supporting the endosymbiotic theory of their origin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The movement of water molecules from a region of high water potential to a region of low water potential through a selectively permeable membrane is called
questions.explanation: Osmosis specifically describes the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane along a water-potential gradient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: A plant cell placed in a hypertonic solution will most likely undergo
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution, water leaves the plant cell by osmosis, causing the protoplast to shrink away from the cell wall, a condition called plasmolysis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes a prokaryotic cell from a eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles, unlike eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The organelle responsible for packaging and modifying proteins for secretion out of the cell is the
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins received from the rough endoplasmic reticulum into vesicles for secretion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which process describes the net movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration without the use of metabolic energy?
questions.explanation: Diffusion is a passive process driven by the concentration gradient and does not require ATP, unlike active transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Enzymes are best described as
options: biological catalysts that are mostly proteins
inorganic ions required in trace amounts
questions.explanation: Enzymes are globular proteins that speed up biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy without being consumed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: An increase in temperature beyond an enzyme's optimum generally causes its activity to
options: decrease sharply as the enzyme denatures
double for every 10 degree rise without limit
questions.explanation: Beyond the optimum temperature, the enzyme's tertiary structure is disrupted (denaturation), destroying the active site and sharply reducing activity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is a monosaccharide?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide), whereas sucrose is a disaccharide and starch and cellulose are polysaccharides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The basic building blocks of proteins are
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked together by peptide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Mitosis results in the formation of
options: two daughter cells with half the chromosome number
two daughter cells genetically identical to the parent cell
questions.explanation: Mitosis is a nuclear division producing two genetically identical diploid daughter cells, used for growth and repair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which stage of mitosis is characterised by the alignment of chromosomes at the equatorial plate?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, spindle fibres align chromosomes at the cell's equator in preparation for separation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The site of aerobic respiration in a eukaryotic cell is the
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion houses the enzymes of the Krebs cycle and electron transport chain that generate ATP aerobically.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Active transport differs from diffusion mainly because active transport
options: always moves substances down a concentration gradient
requires metabolic energy and can move substances against a concentration gradient
questions.explanation: Active transport uses ATP to move substances from a region of lower to higher concentration, unlike passive diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following organelles is responsible for intracellular digestion in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down worn-out organelles, food particles and foreign material within the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The fluid mosaic model describes the structure of the
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic bilayer of phospholipids with embedded, freely moving proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is true of a red blood cell placed in distilled water?
options: It swells and may burst due to water entering by osmosis
It shrinks due to water leaving by osmosis
questions.explanation: Distilled water is hypotonic to the cell contents, so water enters the red blood cell by osmosis, causing it to swell and potentially haemolyse.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Meiosis is significant in sexually reproducing organisms mainly because it
options: produces cells identical to the parent cell
halves the chromosome number and introduces genetic variation
doubles the chromosome number in gametes
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces haploid gametes and, through crossing over and independent assortment, generates genetic variation among offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which pigment, found in chloroplasts, is primarily responsible for absorbing light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, mainly in the red and blue regions of the spectrum, driving the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The cell wall of a typical plant cell is composed mainly of
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are composed mainly of cellulose, a structural polysaccharide that provides rigidity and support.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best describes osmotic pressure in relation to plant cells?
options: It is the pressure exerted by dissolved gases only
It is the force exerted by the cell wall against the protoplast
It only occurs in dead plant cells
It is the pressure that must be applied to prevent net water entry into the cell
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure is the pressure required to stop the net movement of water into a solution by osmosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following statements about nucleic acids is correct?
options: Both DNA and RNA contain thymine
DNA is single stranded while RNA is double stranded
DNA contains deoxyribose sugar while RNA contains ribose sugar
DNA is found only in the cytoplasm
questions.explanation: DNA's sugar component is deoxyribose, while RNA contains ribose; DNA is typically double stranded and RNA single stranded.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which type of tissue in flowering plants is primarily responsible for the transport of water and mineral salts?
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels and tracheids conduct water and dissolved mineral salts upward from the roots to the rest of the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In humans, the exchange of gases occurs across the walls of the
questions.explanation: Alveoli are thin-walled, richly capillarised air sacs that provide a large surface area for the diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery is unusual among arteries in carrying deoxygenated blood, from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The chamber of the human heart with the thickest muscular wall is the
questions.explanation: The left ventricle must pump blood at high pressure around the entire body, so its wall is the thickest of the four chambers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which enzyme, secreted in saliva, begins the digestion of starch in the mouth?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) hydrolyses starch into maltose, initiating carbohydrate digestion in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The organ primarily responsible for the deamination of excess amino acids in humans is the
questions.explanation: The liver deaminates excess amino acids, converting the amino group into urea, which is then excreted by the kidneys.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The functional and structural unit of the kidney responsible for filtration is the
questions.explanation: Each nephron consists of a glomerulus and renal tubule that together filter blood and process the filtrate into urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the process of ultrafiltration in the kidney?
options: Urea is actively secreted into the glomerulus
Glucose is filtered out and never reabsorbed
Water is reabsorbed into the blood at the loop of Henle only
High pressure forces small molecules from the blood into the Bowman's capsule
questions.explanation: In the glomerulus, high hydrostatic pressure forces water and small solutes out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule, forming the glomerular filtrate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The main respiratory pigment found in human red blood cells is
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin, an iron-containing protein in red blood cells, binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it to respiring tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Peristalsis in the alimentary canal refers to
options: the storage of bile in the gall bladder
the absorption of digested food into the blood
wave-like muscular contractions that push food along the gut
the chemical breakdown of food by enzymes
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic, wave-like contraction and relaxation of gut muscles that propels food along the alimentary canal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which hormone, secreted by the pancreas, lowers blood glucose level by promoting its uptake and storage as glycogen?
questions.explanation: Insulin stimulates cells, particularly liver and muscle cells, to absorb glucose and convert it into glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The skeletal joint that allows movement in only one plane, as seen at the elbow, is a
questions.explanation: A hinge joint, like the elbow and knee, permits movement in a single plane, similar to the motion of a door hinge.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct pathway of a nerve impulse in a simple reflex arc?
options: Effector, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, receptor
Sensory neurone, receptor, effector, motor neurone
Receptor, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, effector
Receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector
questions.explanation: A typical reflex arc transmits impulses from a receptor through a sensory neurone, a relay neurone in the spinal cord, then a motor neurone to an effector.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The part of the human brain primarily responsible for coordinating balance and muscular movement is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates fine motor movement, posture and balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which structure in the leaf regulates the rate of transpiration by controlling the opening and closing of pores?
questions.explanation: Guard cells surround the stomatal pore and change shape to open or close it, thereby regulating gaseous exchange and water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The process by which plants lose water vapour mainly through their stomata is known as
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from aerial plant parts, chiefly through open stomata on leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Homeostasis in mammals refers to the
options: maintenance of a stable internal environment despite external changes
breakdown of glucose to release energy
questions.explanation: Homeostasis describes the physiological mechanisms that keep internal conditions such as temperature, pH and water balance relatively constant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the role of the loop of Henle in the nephron?
options: It creates a concentration gradient that enables water reabsorption and urine concentration
It secretes hormones that regulate blood pressure
It filters blood plasma into the Bowman's capsule
It stores urine before it passes to the bladder
questions.explanation: The loop of Henle sets up an osmotic gradient in the medulla through the countercurrent multiplier mechanism, allowing the collecting duct to reabsorb water and concentrate urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Vasoconstriction of skin blood vessels in response to cold conditions helps the body to
options: conserve heat by reducing blood flow near the skin surface
increase heat loss through the skin
questions.explanation: Vasoconstriction narrows skin capillaries, reducing blood flow to the surface and minimising heat loss to conserve body heat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The exchange surfaces of the lungs, gills and small intestine share which common structural feature that improves efficiency?
options: A large surface area relative to volume
questions.explanation: Efficient exchange surfaces are characterised by a large surface area, thin walls and good blood supply, which together speed diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following gases diffuses out of the blood into the alveoli to be exhaled?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, a waste product of respiration, diffuses from the blood, which has a higher concentration of it, into the alveolar air to be exhaled.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The role of bile, produced by the liver, in digestion is mainly to
options: emulsify fats into smaller droplets for enzyme action
neutralise excess alkalinity in the duodenum
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies large fat globules into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area available for lipase to act on.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which structure in a woody plant stem is responsible for secondary growth in girth?
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium is a lateral meristem that produces new xylem and phloem cells, increasing the diameter of the stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In flowering plants, the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower is called
questions.explanation: Self-pollination occurs when pollen from the anther lands on the stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which structure in the flower develops into the fruit after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the ovary wall develops into the fruit wall (pericarp), while the ovules become seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Double fertilisation, a process unique to flowering plants, results in the formation of the
questions.explanation: In double fertilisation, one male gamete fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, while the other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the triploid endosperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In the human male reproductive system, sperm cells are produced in the
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis, the production of sperm, occurs within the seminiferous tubules found in the testes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Fertilisation in humans normally occurs in the
questions.explanation: The sperm typically meets and fertilises the ovum within the fallopian tube, after which the zygote travels to the uterus for implantation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which hormone is primarily responsible for maintaining the uterine lining during early pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Progesterone, secreted first by the corpus luteum and later by the placenta, maintains the endometrium, supporting the pregnancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Vegetative propagation in plants is a form of
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation produces new plants from vegetative parts such as stems, roots or leaves without the fusion of gametes, making it asexual.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is an adaptation of wind-pollinated flowers?
options: Small, dull petals and large amounts of light, powdery pollen
Large, brightly coloured petals and scent
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers typically have small, inconspicuous petals, feathery stigmas, and produce large quantities of light pollen suited for wind dispersal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In humans, the process by which a fertilised egg becomes embedded in the uterine wall is called
questions.explanation: Implantation is the process by which the blastocyst attaches to and embeds itself into the endometrium of the uterus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Metamorphosis in insects such as the housefly, which passes through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages, is described as
questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis involves four distinct stages (egg, larva, pupa, adult), with the pupa undergoing a radical transformation, as seen in flies and butterflies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best describes external fertilisation, as seen in most fish and amphibians?
options: Fusion of gametes occurs outside the body of the female, usually in water
Fusion of gametes occurs inside the female's reproductive tract
Fertilisation occurs within a shelled egg outside water
questions.explanation: In external fertilisation, males and females release gametes into the surrounding water, where fusion of sperm and egg occurs outside the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The placenta in mammals primarily functions to
options: allow exchange of nutrients, gases and waste between mother and foetus
questions.explanation: The placenta is a specialised organ that allows diffusion of oxygen, nutrients and waste products between the maternal and foetal blood supplies without them mixing directly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following floral parts produces pollen grains?
questions.explanation: The anther, borne at the tip of the stamen filament, contains pollen sacs in which pollen grains (male gametophytes) are produced.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In the menstrual cycle, ovulation is triggered mainly by a surge in
questions.explanation: A sharp surge in luteinising hormone (LH) midway through the cycle triggers the rupture of the mature follicle and release of the egg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of these is an example of asexual reproduction in simple organisms?
questions.explanation: Binary fission, where a single parent cell divides into two identical daughter cells, is a common form of asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms like Amoeba.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: A cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt), where tallness is dominant, is expected to produce offspring in the phenotypic ratio
questions.explanation: A monohybrid cross between two heterozygotes (Tt x Tt) produces a genotypic ratio of 1TT:2Tt:1tt, giving a phenotypic ratio of 3 dominant : 1 recessive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: An individual with two different alleles for a particular gene, such as Aa, is said to be
questions.explanation: An organism carrying two different alleles for a gene (one dominant, one recessive) is described as heterozygous for that trait.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is the physical, observable expression of an organism's genetic makeup?
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable characteristics of an organism, resulting from the interaction of its genotype with the environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In humans, colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive trait carried on the X chromosome. A colour-blind man marries a woman who is homozygous normal. What proportion of their sons will be colour blind?
options: None, since sons receive their X chromosome from the mother
questions.explanation: Sons inherit their single X chromosome from their mother; since she is homozygous normal, all sons will receive a normal allele and will not be colour blind.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Gregor Mendel's Law of Segregation states that
options: genes for different traits always assort independently of each other
the two alleles for a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete carries only one allele
dominant alleles always mask recessive alleles completely in all cases
offspring always resemble one parent exactly
questions.explanation: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that allele pairs separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives only one allele from each pair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: A change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA, which may alter an organism's phenotype, is called a
questions.explanation: A mutation is any change in the base sequence of DNA, which can arise spontaneously or be induced by mutagens, sometimes altering the phenotype.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Down syndrome in humans is caused by
options: the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 21
a point mutation in a single gene
a deletion of part of the X chromosome
the loss of an entire autosome
questions.explanation: Down syndrome results from trisomy 21, a chromosomal abnormality where an individual has three copies of chromosome 21 instead of two.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals (AaBb x AaBb), assuming independent assortment, the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes produces four phenotype classes in the ratio 9:3:3:1 when the genes assort independently.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The complete set of hereditary information carried by an organism is referred to as its
questions.explanation: The genome is the entire set of genetic material, including all genes, present in an organism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best explains why identical (monozygotic) twins have the same genotype?
options: They share the same placenta but different genomes
They result from the fusion of two sperm cells
They develop from two separately fertilised eggs
They develop from a single fertilised egg that splits into two embryos
questions.explanation: Monozygotic twins arise when a single zygote splits early in development into two embryos, so both twins share identical genetic material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: A test cross is performed by crossing an individual of unknown genotype with an individual that is
questions.explanation: A test cross uses a homozygous recessive individual because the resulting offspring's phenotypes directly reveal whether the tested organism is homozygous or heterozygous dominant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of incomplete dominance?
options: A cross between red and white snapdragons producing pink offspring
A cross where the recessive trait is never expressed
A cross producing offspring identical to only one parent
A cross between tall and short pea plants producing all tall offspring
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype, as seen when red and white snapdragons produce pink-flowered offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The structural unit of a chromosome that carries the code for a specific protein or trait is called a
questions.explanation: A gene is a discrete segment of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a specific protein or functional RNA product, determining a trait.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Within a food chain, organisms that manufacture their own food using sunlight are known as
questions.explanation: Producers, mainly green plants and algae, are autotrophs that convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis, forming the base of most food chains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The role of decomposers such as bacteria and fungi in an ecosystem is mainly to
options: break down dead organic matter and release nutrients back into the environment
convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia only
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste, releasing locked-up nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen compounds back into the ecosystem for reuse.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In an ecological pyramid of numbers, energy is progressively lost between trophic levels mainly through
questions.explanation: At each trophic level, a large proportion of energy is lost as heat through respiration and other metabolic activities, explaining the pyramid shape of energy flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: A community of interacting organisms together with their non-living physical environment is called a(n)
questions.explanation: An ecosystem comprises the biotic community of organisms and the abiotic factors (soil, water, climate) with which they interact.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best defines a population in ecological terms?
options: A group of different species living together
All the living and non-living things in an area
A group of organisms of the same species living in a given area at the same time
The physical area where an organism lives
questions.explanation: A population consists of individuals of one species occupying a particular area at a given time, capable of interbreeding.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The process by which atmospheric nitrogen is converted into a form usable by plants, largely through the action of soil bacteria, is called
questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation converts inert atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or related compounds that plants can absorb and use, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which relationship describes an association where one organism benefits and the other is unaffected?
questions.explanation: In commensalism, one species benefits from the association while the other neither benefits nor is harmed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The relationship between a tapeworm and the human host it lives in is best described as
questions.explanation: A tapeworm benefits by obtaining nutrients from its host while harming the host, which is the defining feature of parasitism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a biotic factor affecting an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors are living components of the environment, such as predation, competition and disease, as opposed to abiotic factors like rainfall and temperature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The continuous cycling of carbon between the atmosphere, living organisms and the environment mainly involves the processes of
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to build organic compounds, while respiration and combustion return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere, driving the carbon cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following practices most directly contributes to soil erosion?
options: Deforestation and removal of vegetation cover
questions.explanation: Removing vegetation exposes the soil surface to wind and water, greatly increasing the rate of soil erosion, unlike practices such as afforestation that protect the soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Two species that require the same limited resource, such as food or space, within a habitat are said to be in
questions.explanation: Competition occurs when two or more organisms or species vie for the same limited resource, potentially reducing the fitness of both.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: In a typical grassland food chain: grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, hawk; the snake occupies which trophic level?
questions.explanation: Counting grass as producer, grasshopper as primary consumer, frog as secondary consumer, the snake that eats the frog is the tertiary consumer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which gas, released mainly from burning fossil fuels, is most closely associated with the enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas whose atmospheric concentration has risen sharply due to fossil fuel combustion, contributing to global warming.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: An area's carrying capacity refers to
options: the rate at which a population grows without limit
the maximum population size an environment can sustainably support
the minimum number of predators needed
the total number of species present
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population size that a given environment can sustain indefinitely given its available resources.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Charles Darwin's theory of evolution is primarily based on the mechanism of
questions.explanation: Darwin proposed that organisms with favourable variations are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing those traits to offspring, a process called natural selection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which scientist proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics, later shown to be largely incorrect?
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime, such as a giraffe stretching its neck, could be passed to offspring, a theory not supported by modern genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Structures such as the forelimbs of a human, whale and bat, which have a similar basic bone structure but different functions, are described as
questions.explanation: Homologous structures share a common underlying structure inherited from a shared ancestor, even though they may serve different functions, providing evidence for evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Body structures that are reduced and no longer serve their original function, such as the human appendix, are termed
questions.explanation: Vestigial structures are remnants of organs that were functional in ancestral species but have become reduced or non-functional over evolutionary time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The peppered moth (Biston betularia) population shift from light to dark forms during the industrial revolution in England is a classic example of
options: natural selection in response to environmental change
questions.explanation: As pollution darkened tree bark, dark moths were better camouflaged from predators than light moths, so natural selection favoured the dark form, shifting the population's frequency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following provides direct evidence of evolutionary change preserved in rock strata?
questions.explanation: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms found in sedimentary rock layers, providing a direct historical record of evolutionary change over time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The process by which two unrelated species evolve similar structures independently due to similar environmental pressures is called
questions.explanation: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated organisms independently evolve analogous structures, such as the wings of birds and insects, due to similar selective pressures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Analogous structures, such as the wings of a bird and the wings of a butterfly, are similar in function but
options: differ in evolutionary origin and basic structure
are found only in closely related species
questions.explanation: Analogous structures perform similar functions but evolved independently in unrelated lineages, so they differ in their underlying structure and evolutionary origin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: According to modern evolutionary theory, new alleles that introduce genetic variation into a population primarily arise through
options: the survival of the fittest alone
questions.explanation: Mutation is the ultimate source of new genetic variation, upon which natural selection and other evolutionary forces can then act.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: The formation of a new species from an ancestral population that becomes geographically isolated is known as
questions.explanation: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations of a species are separated by a geographic barrier, evolve independently, and eventually become reproductively isolated as distinct species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Adaptive radiation, as seen in Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands, refers to
options: the merging of two species into one
the mutation of a gene with no ecological effect
the extinction of a species due to competition
the diversification of a single ancestral species into many species occupying different niches
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation describes the rapid evolution of many species from a single ancestor as they adapt to fill different available ecological niches, as seen in the varied beak shapes of Darwin's finches.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which of the following best describes 'survival of the fittest' as used in evolutionary biology?
options: Organisms best suited to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce
Only the physically strongest organisms in a population survive
Fitness refers only to an organism's physical strength
All organisms in a population have an equal chance of survival
questions.explanation: In evolutionary terms, 'fitness' refers to reproductive success; organisms whose traits are best suited to their environment tend to survive and pass on their genes more successfully.
